festivals.name: Outside Lands 2026
festivals.why: Rüfüs Du Sol + The xx headline the on-taste end; Charli xcx, The Strokes, Turnstile, Empire of the Sun broaden it. ~2 months out, travel weekend. 3-day GA from ~$569.

festivals.name: Daisy Chain Fields (Olivia Rodrigo)
festivals.location: Great Park Live, Irvine (OC — ~45 mi, worth the drive)
festivals.why: Olivia Rodrigo's first festival — a one-day, all-women lineup (Chappell Roan, Doechii, Mitski, The Breeders, Bikini Kill, Garbage, Santigold + special guests Stevie Nicks, Karen O, Sarah McLachlan), 100% of net proceeds to women/girls nonprofits. Off the core house/techno lane, but a marquee must-know — and squarely on-taste for the Lori profile (she tracks Olivia Rodrigo + Mitski). Tickets via Front Gate; from $250.

festivals.name: CRSSD Festival — Fall 2026
festivals.why: SD is a drive, but this is festival-tier and on-taste — Disclosure, Chris Lake, Groove Armada (DJ set), Helena Hauff, Ben UFO, I Hate Models, Mathame, Carlita, salute. House/ techno/melodic, European lean, waterfront, 21+. NOTE: same weekend as Portola (SF) — can't do both; pick one.

festivals.name: Portola 2026
festivals.why: THE one for you — electronic-forward with DESPACIO (James Murphy + 2ManyDJs sound system), Four Tet, Soulwax, Groove Armada, DJ Shadow, Fatboy Slim, Skepta, plus Robyn, Tiësto, Swedish House Mafia. European/house energy in a warehouse-pier setting. 2-day ~$380.

festivals.name: Coachella 2027
festivals.why: Advance GA already sold out (~$549–599); lineup typically drops Sept 2026–Jan 2027. Worth tracking the lineup announce to decide if a resale is worth it.

festivals.name: GALA Festival (London) — 2027 edition
festivals.why: Quintessential European house/disco day-fest (2026: Seth Troxler, Todd Terje, Call Super, DJ Seinfeld). On-taste, but not timely — only bubble up when 2027 presale/lineup drops.

dining.name: Pasjoli

dining.name: Kassi

dining.name: San Laurel

dining.name: Calabra

dining.name: Found Oyster

dining.name: Bar Restaurant
dining.notes: Pink-hued, 'strange and fantastic' modern French. Intimate date-night; books up. Sunset Junction, walkable.

dining.name: Sogo Roll Bar
dining.notes: Handroll bar from the Sushi Note team — creative, high-quality fish. Counter seats. Eastside.

dining.name: Lolo Wine Bar
dining.notes: Low-key neighborhood wine bar with a great patio + shareable pasta. Walkable from home.

dining.name: Marco Polo
dining.notes: Outdoor-focused Italian — linguini vongole, gin-arugula cocktails. Patio date-night. Home turf.

dining.name: Clark Street Bakery
dining.notes: Echo Park bakery — caramelized kouign-amann, Nordic breakfast platters. Daytime/casual.

dining.name: Kismet Rotisserie
dining.notes: Casual rotisserie next to Kismet — roast chicken on pita, veg sides. Easy weeknight. Eastside.

dining.name: Jeff's Table
dining.notes: Cult deli hidden behind a liquor store — pastrami, specialty turkey. Lunch. Eastside.

dining.name: Yang's Kitchen
dining.notes: Order-at-counter Taiwanese-Chinese — braised pork rice, beef scallion wraps. SGV-adjacent.

dining.name: Sonmari
dining.notes: Silver Lake handroll spot — inventive DIY rolls (gochujang eel, 'banh mi' albacore). Walkable.

dining.name: Bar Di Bello
dining.notes: Low-lit Milanese-style aperitivo bar — cutlets, branzino, antipasti. Date-night. Home turf.

dining.name: Holbox
dining.notes: Game-changing Mexican seafood stall in Mercado La Paloma — aguachiles, tostadas. Michelin Bib-tier value (confirm). Walk-up.

dining.name: Quarter Sheets
dining.notes: Thick pan-style pizza + great wine list. Bib Gourmand value. Echo Park — walkable from home.

dining.name: Pizzeria Bianco
dining.notes: Chris Bianco's LA outpost (Row DTLA) — among the country's best pizza. Bib Gourmand. Confirm exact address.

dining.name: Sushi Note
dining.notes: Sushi-and-wine bar (team behind Sogo Roll Bar). Valley — a destination, not walkable.

dining.name: Santo
dining.notes: Japanese-Mexican nigiri/handrolls + sake & wine, Sunset Junction. Home turf; next to Bar Seco. (Santō)

dining.name: Bar Seco
dining.notes: Natural wine bar + small plates (CDMX/Madrid/Japan), spills onto Sunset. Walk-in/sidewalk seats. Next to Santo. (aka Seco)

dining.name: Superba
dining.notes: ARI'S ABSOLUTE FAVORITE — food + ambiance, the patio especially (also great inside). Superba Food + Bread, Lincoln Blvd. Westside — worth the drive.

dining.name: L&E Oyster Bar
dining.notes: Silver Lake oyster bar; the upstairs bar is the chill walk-in move. Home turf.

dining.name: Pijja Palace
dining.notes: Indian-Italian sports bar — pizza, pasta, cricket on the TVs. Very popular (hard rez / walk-in bar). Silver Lake, home turf.

dining.name: Night + Market Song
dining.notes: Kris Yenbamroong's fiery northern Thai on Sunset. Walk-in friendly. Home turf.

dining.name: Momed
dining.notes: Mediterranean — mezze, wraps, bowls. Atwater Village (also Beverly Hills). Eastside, easy.

dining.name: Bar Siesta
dining.notes: New Spanish tapas + all-Spanish wine bar (Heather Sperling team). On-taste wine bar, home turf.

dining.name: Atrium
dining.notes: Playful, vaguely-French cooking from Douglas Rankin in the old Malo space, Sunset Junction. New. Home turf.

dining.name: Bowery Bungalow
dining.notes: Modern Mediterranean from George Abou-Daoud in the former Sompun Thai. New, home turf.

dining.name: Frank n Franks

artist_notes.note: LA selector behind the Direct Drive party series — a self-described 'Chicago soul' deep house/club-music digger who's shared bills with Ariel Zetina and Introspekt on the DTLA warehouse circuit.

enrichment.curator_note: A real LuckyMe-label showcase hiding behind a TBA Koreatown address — Jacques Greene's moody, warped garage is the draw, and bahar khadem's Direct Drive credentials make the rest of the bill trustworthy too.

artist_notes.name: Black Moth Super Rainbow
artist_notes.note: Tobacco-fronted Pittsburgh outfit — vocoder-heavy, hazy psychedelic pop over fuzzed analog synths; a cult-favorite band, not a nostalgia act despite the vintage-synth sound. ('Psych' isn't yet in the subgenre vocab; flagging rather than coining a tag.)

artist_notes.name: Giant Day
artist_notes.note: Elephant 6-affiliated post-punk/art-rock duo (Derek Almstead of Olivia Tremor Control/of Montreal + Emily Growden) — psych-funk, synth-forward; the first official new E6 band in 15+ years.

enrichment.curator_note: Black Moth Super Rainbow's woozy, vocoder-drenched psych-pop is a genuinely different flavor from the house/techno lane — good for a stranger, warmer Friday at the Belasco, and Giant Day's Elephant 6 pedigree makes the opener worth showing up early for.

events.genre: leftfield, downtempo, house, breaks, drum and bass, jungle

artist_notes.name: NAP (MX)
artist_notes.note: Daniel Rincón — Colombian-born, Vancouver/Montreal-raised (1080p/Mood Hut crew) producer now based in Mexico City; blends Latin club, cumbia/sonidero and dubby ambient techno, and runs the ACA label focused on South American electronic music.

artist_notes.name: Hashman Deejay
artist_notes.note: Tanner Matt — Vancouver deep-house/dub producer in the Mood Hut orbit (collaborates with PLO Man, Pender Street Steppers); raw, outsider house and ambient dub, deliberately low-profile — no interviews, lets the records talk.

artist_notes.name: Luke Mele
artist_notes.note: LA-based selector with a long-running NTS Radio show spanning Balearic house, dub techno, ambient and trip-hop — a genuine home-listening digger.

enrichment.curator_note: NAP and Hashman both come out of Vancouver's Mood Hut world, so this reads as a slow-burn, dubby, textural night rather than a peak-time one — the Pomona trek is the real cost of entry.
enrichment.description: Night Moves afterhours DJ night at Homage Brewing, Pomona, with NAP (MX), Hashman Deejay and Luke Mele (10pm+).

events.title: Heat Advisory: Unofficial Hard Summer Afters Day 1 (21+)
events.detail: Open-air fest HARD Summer returns with a globe-trotting line-up boasting Tokischa, salute, Charlotte de Witte, Zack Fox, Shygirl, VTSS and hometown heroes CQUESTT and Dj Warning.

artist_notes.name: Anetha
artist_notes.note: French techno DJ/producer out of the Paris scene — raw, physical peak-time sets, a fixture of the current European festival-techno wave.

artist_notes.name: VTSS
artist_notes.note: Polish producer known for hard, industrial/EBM-tinged techno — harder-edged than the Amelie Lens/Charlotte de Witte lane but the same festival-techno circuit.

artist_notes.name: Brutalismus 3000
artist_notes.note: German techno duo mixing 90s rave euphoria with hardgroove — part of the Berlin-adjacent revival crew getting big US festival bookings.

artist_notes.name: Interplanetary Criminal
artist_notes.note: UK producer bridging bassline and the UK garage revival, out of the Manchester scene.

artist_notes.name: Sammy Virji
artist_notes.note: UK garage/bassline producer at the center of the current UKG resurgence.

artist_notes.name: Nick León
artist_notes.note: Miami producer fusing reggaeton/dembow rhythms with house and techno — released on TraTraTrax.

artist_notes.name: Andy C
artist_notes.note: UK drum & bass legend, Ram Records founder — one of DnB's most enduring headline draws.

artist_notes.name: Maceo Plex
artist_notes.note: Veteran tech-house/techno producer (aka Maetrik), Ellum Audio boss, long-running Ibiza/festival mainstay.

artist_notes.name: Confidence Man
artist_notes.note: Australian dance-pop group with a theatrical, costumed live show — festival-circuit favorite, more pop spectacle than DJ set.

artist_notes.name: Amelie Lens
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno star, Exhale label — tracked name; driving, hypnotic peak-time techno with real European club credibility (see also her own Grand Park date this batch).

artist_notes.name: Boys Noize
artist_notes.note: Berlin electro/techno veteran (Alex Ridha) — distorted, industrial-leaning club music going back to the mid-2000s Boysnoize Records run; still a reliably weird, high-energy set.

artist_notes.name: bahar khadem
artist_notes.note: LA selector behind the Direct Drive party series — a self-described 'Chicago soul' deep house/club-music digger who's shared bills with Ariel Zetina and Introspekt on the DTLA warehouse circuit.

artist_notes.name: Star Eyes
artist_notes.note: NYC-via-LA bass polymath — Trouble & Bass crew co-founder turned Chaos Clan/Warp Mode; jungle, UK garage and Baltimore/Jersey club roots, played Fabric London and Outlook Festival.

artist_notes.name: Charlotte de Witte
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno powerhouse, KNTXT label boss — hard, hypnotic peak-time techno; a tracked name and one of the strongest bookings on this lineup.

artist_notes.name: Chris Lorenzo
artist_notes.note: UK bass/house producer, Half Baked label — tracked name; UK garage-inflected, bass-heavy house.

artist_notes.name: DJ Seinfeld
artist_notes.note: Swedish-Argentine producer (Armand Jakobsson) who pioneered 'lo-fi house' — tracked name; hazy, nostalgic house that's a shade more tasteful than most of this bill.

artist_notes.name: Etari
artist_notes.note: LA-based (Orange County-raised) producer and AUNTIE co-founder — house through trance and techno, with releases on 100% Silk; regular on the Lights Down Low/HARD Summer circuit.

artist_notes.name: Hannah Laing
artist_notes.note: Scottish DJ/producer on the UK hard-house/hardcore-revival wave — high-BPM, rave-nostalgic tech house.

artist_notes.name: fun2bjane
artist_notes.note: LA DJ (Jane O'Conner) — INCOGNITO and Sensory Signal resident who's played HARD Summer and Skyline; sets bounce between sassy house/techno and late-'90s prog/trance.

artist_notes.name: Mau P
artist_notes.note: Dutch producer of 'Drugs From Amsterdam' fame — tracked name; big-room tech house with a raw, jacking edge.

artist_notes.name: Shane Thomas
artist_notes.note: LA producer/DJ, Ace Hotel-residency host of the party blush! — experimental house and techno spliced with reggaeton, dancehall and ballroom edits.

artist_notes.name: Oscar Osorio
artist_notes.note: Groovers Ball resident, regularly paired with DJ LIGMA (they've released a joint EP together) — same bangin' rave/techno lane as the rest of the crew.

artist_notes.name: Pegassi
artist_notes.note: Belgian producer (Sam Huybrecht) running his own label/party series Sweet Nothing — a deliberately 'post-genre' set that swings between trance, techno, eurodance and house rather than staying in a lane. Closer to a big-room selector than a groove/disco DJ.

artist_notes.name: salute
artist_notes.note: Austrian-born, Brighton-based producer signed to Ninja Tune — fast, soulful house with a UK garage-adjacent bounce; has been playing bigger US festival stages (EDC) this year.

artist_notes.name: Shygirl
artist_notes.note: UK rapper/vocalist and NUXXE co-founder — hyperpop-adjacent club music, Sega Bodega/Arca collaborator; more art-club than DJ set.

artist_notes.name: Tiga
artist_notes.note: Montreal electro-house institution (Turbo Recordings) — tongue-in-cheek, disco-inflected electro; a real name for the older end of this bill.

artist_notes.name: Vintage Culture
artist_notes.note: Brazilian tech-house export, Solotoko boss — tracked name; huge festival draw, big-room but genuinely well-selected house.

enrichment.curator_note: The techno/house names on here are genuinely great — Charlotte de Witte, Amelie Lens, Mau P, Vintage Culture, Anetha, VTSS — but they're buried in an 80-deep multigenre HARD afters bill that's mostly bass/EDM mega-rave energy, not the rooftop-groove lane. Worth it only if you're going for those specific sets.
enrichment.description: Unofficial single-day HARD Summer afters at Hollywood Park Grounds (Inglewood), an 80-plus-name, all-day-into-night bill spanning techno, house, tech-house, bass, drum & bass and mainstream EDM.

events.title: WORK x TSSRCT present: Civic Instruction [LIVE], Hadone, UFO95 [LIVE] & GiGi
events.detail: Performing as Civic Instruction, Hadone and UFO95 will put on a live hardware set full of 90's-flavoured techno.

artist_notes.name: Hadone
artist_notes.note: French producer, one half of the live hardware duo Civic Instruction — raw, 90s-flavored techno.

artist_notes.name: UFO95
artist_notes.note: French producer, the other half of Civic Instruction with Hadone — dark, hypnotic hardware-techno live sets; the pair just launched their own label, TSSRCT.

artist_notes.name: GiGi
artist_notes.note: LA acid/techno DJ (Fixvtion founder), part of the INCOGNITO/Raw Cuts underground-techno orbit.

enrichment.curator_note: An RA pick for a reason — Hadone and UFO95's Civic Instruction is a genuine live hardware set (not a laptop DJ set with a fog machine), and 90s-style raw techno at a TBA afterhours location is exactly the kind of night worth staying out for.
enrichment.description: WORK x TSSRCT afterhours (TBA location, 11pm-6am) with a live hardware techno set from Civic Instruction (Hadone & UFO95) plus GiGi.

events.title: BAILE WORLD ft DJ Slugo
events.genre: reggaeton, dembow, gqom, baile funk, miami bass, jersey club
events.detail: A leading figure in Chicago's ghetto house movement, DJ Slugo brings decades of raw, high-impact dance music to Los Angeles.

artist_notes.name: DJ Slugo
artist_notes.note: Chicago ghetto-house/footwork pioneer, founding Dance Mania crew alongside DJ Deeon and Paul Johnson — raw, high-BPM, chant-hook club tracks; the sound Daft Punk sampled on 'Teachers.'

enrichment.curator_note: Baile World is one of LA's best global-club rooms (founded by DJ CQUESTT, built around femme/POC selectors), and landing a Dance Mania originator like DJ Slugo is a real coup — footwork/ghetto-house rather than straight house, so know what you're walking into, but it'll move.

events.title: Certified Groovers w/ Demuir, Juliet Mendoza, Force Placement

artist_notes.name: Demuir
artist_notes.note: Detroit-born, Atlanta-based tech-house DJ/producer on his own Sound Explorer imprint — a fixture of Beatport's charts, prolific and reliably jacking.

artist_notes.name: Juliet Mendoza
artist_notes.note: LA underground house DJ and founder of Jill's House, rooted in the '90s LA house scene (Arena, Carnival) — has shared decks with Peggy Gou and Hot Since 82; deep, soulful, melodic sets.

artist_notes.name: Force Placement
artist_notes.note: LA techno DJ/producer (Jason James), co-founder of The Black Lodge collective/label — ranges soulful house to acid techno, a genuinely respected name in the local underground.

artist_notes.name: Ian Llorens
artist_notes.note: Certified Groovers resident, LA-based (Puerto Rico-born) — rhythm-forward house/techno selector, also plays as O God / Soundprism.

enrichment.curator_note: An 8-hour DTLA warehouse booking with real range — Demuir's chart-topping tech-house pairs with two proper underground names in Juliet Mendoza (deep 90s-rooted LA house) and Force Placement (acid techno, Black Lodge crew).
enrichment.description: Certified Groovers all-night warehouse party (10pm-8am) in DTLA with Demuir, Juliet Mendoza and Force Placement, location TBA.

events.title: FLOAT Rooftop Pool Party ft. Chambord [2-8 PM]

artist_notes.name: Chambord
artist_notes.note: LA-based DJ/production duo — eclectic, melodic sets pulling in world-music textures alongside more hypnotic electronic passages; a reasonable fit for FLOAT's rooftop-groove daytime format.

enrichment.curator_note: Same FLOAT rooftop-pool formula as the Wisternoff date a week earlier — Chambord's a local, eclectic-melodic booking rather than a marquee name, but the setting alone earns it a look.
enrichment.description: FLOAT rooftop pool party at Level 8 DTLA (2-8pm) with local duo Chambord.

artist_notes.name: Scotty Boy
artist_notes.note: Vegas-based house veteran (25+ years, three Billboard Dance #1s) and founder of DTLA's long-running 'Deep House Brunch' — plays crowd-friendly deep/jackin' house and nu-disco edits, more festival-polish than underground digger.

enrichment.curator_note: Same Scotty Boy energy you'd expect from him anywhere — reliable jackin'-house-and-disco-edits, and free entry makes it an easy add to a Koreatown night rather than a destination on its own.

artist_notes.name: DJ Seinfeld
artist_notes.note: Swedish-Argentine producer (Armand Jakobsson) who pioneered 'lo-fi house' — tracked name; hazy, nostalgic house that's a shade more tasteful than most of this bill.

artist_notes.note: LA-based DJ and radio host known for genre-blending, eclectic sets rather than a single lane — less pedigree info available, so treat as the wildcard on this bill.

enrichment.curator_note: Free RSVP industry showcase at Beatport's LA HQ during HARD Summer weekend — DJ Seinfeld's hazy lo-fi house next to salute's punchier stuff is a solid pairing for a freebie, just don't expect a proper club room.

artist_notes.name: Shonky
artist_notes.note: Paris house/tech-house lifer (Olivier Ducreux) — a third of the Apollonia trio with Dan Ghenacia and Dyed Soundorom; groovy, stripped-back underground house, well-suited to an extended set.

artist_notes.name: Silky
artist_notes.note: London house/techno DJ mentored by Frankie Knuckles — works the grey zone between deep house and techno, with releases on Culprit and My Favorite Robot.

artist_notes.name: Enzo Muro
artist_notes.note: Peruvian-born, LA-based house/techno selector and a resident of Dialogue itself — patient, flow-first sets; also co-runs the vinyl-only YouKnowWhat label/party.

artist_notes.name: Lubelski
artist_notes.note: LA producer (Jake Lubell) making analog, vinyl-informed house with a wide festival footprint (Lightning in a Bottle, Desert Hearts, Dirtybird Campout) — eclectic and percussive rather than a strict selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Shonky's extended set is the real draw — a founding third of the Apollonia crew doing groovy, stripped-back house — and Dialogue's own resident Enzo Muro plus LA's Lubelski keep the afternoon honest.
enrichment.description: Daytime dance party at DTLA's The Bridge headlined by an extended set from Paris tech-house veteran Shonky, with Silky, Enzo Muro and Lubelski.

events.title: Sunday Sessions LA: Highkin All Night Long (Vinyl Only)
events.venue: 450 S Bixel St, Los Angeles, CA 90017

artist_notes.name: Highkin
artist_notes.note: Moscow-born, LA-based vinyl collector/DJ — a regular in the Sunday Sessions LA rotation.

enrichment.curator_note: Same open-air, single-DJ, all-vinyl format as the rest of the Sunday Sessions run; Highkin's a less known quantity than some of the series' other residents, so this is more about the ritual than the name.
enrichment.description: A vinyl-only, open-air all-night set from DJ Highkin, part of the weekly Sunday Sessions LA series.

artist_notes.name: Lee Foss
artist_notes.note: Chicago-schooled house lifer out of DeKalb, IL — co-founded Hot Creations with Jamie Jones and later launched Repopulate Mars; a real name in modern underground house, not just a big-festival booking.

artist_notes.name: Henry Pope
artist_notes.note: Venice Beach-based producer running his own Genius Loci/Fresh Tracks/Sense labels — Beatport #1 indie-dance and afro-house releases, sets that fold in live musicians.

enrichment.curator_note: Lee Foss headlining is a legit underground-house booking, but Malibu on a random Saturday afternoon is a real haul unless you're already out that way.
enrichment.description: Daytime house party at Cielo Farms in Malibu with Hot Creations/Repopulate Mars co-founder Lee Foss and Henry Pope.

events.title: Bears In Space Lot Party with Warehouse Preservation Society

artist_notes.name: Warehouse Preservation Society
artist_notes.note: LA disco-house DJ duo (TK & Tavish) — dynamic, acid-tinged dancefloor energy; played Glastonbury, Love International and Sunset Campout, one half rooted in '90s SF underground, the other in Venice/Ocean Park hip-hop-to-house.

artist_notes.name: Bears In Space
artist_notes.note: The LA collective behind this very party — Chris Bowen and Victor Rodriguez have run it since 2009, one of the city's longest-standing queer disco/house day parties, historically pulling in guests like DJ Harvey and Horse Meat Disco.

artist_notes.name: Perfect Lovers
artist_notes.note: LA DJ (Celice Monnette) and co-founder of the Mexico City/LA queer warehouse party @pordetroitmx and the Muy Muy label — house and techno with a queer-community throughline.

artist_notes.name: Stacy Christine
artist_notes.note: LA warehouse-scene DJ since 2012 (Music For Dancers, Critter Control, Machine Club lineage) — joyful house into kinetic techno; has opened for DJ Harvey, Moodymann, and Honey Dijon.

enrichment.curator_note: This is the real thing, not a knockoff — Bears in Space has been Silver Lake's queer disco-house day party since 2009 (DJ Harvey and Horse Meat Disco have both played it), walkable from home, and this bill is literally the people who built it — Chris Bowen and Victor Rodriguez themselves, plus Perfect Lovers.
enrichment.description: Bears in Space's recurring queer disco/house day party in the Akbar parking lot, with founders Chris Bowen and Victor Rodriguez, Warehouse Preservation Society, Perfect Lovers, and Stacy Christine.

artist_notes.note: Montreal-born, now LA-based progressive/melodic house duo (Ossama Al Sarraf & Ned Shepard) — Grammy-nominated for their Bruno Mars remix; steady, emotive mid-tempo sets since the early 2010s remix era rather than an underground name.

artist_notes.name: Kasbo
artist_notes.note: Gothenburg producer on ODESZA's Foreign Family Collective — soulful, melody-rich electronic that leans future-bass/downtempo; softer and poppier than the rest of this bill.

artist_notes.name: Massane
artist_notes.note: French melodic-house producer and guitarist — debut EP and album on Lane 8's This Never Happened, plus a release on mau5trap. Guitar-textured, emotive melodic house that sits right next to the Anjunadeep/Lane 8 end of the spectrum.

artist_notes.name: Qrion
artist_notes.note: Japan-born, Austin-based producer on Anjunadeep — shimmering, emotive melodic house; DJ Mag's 2021 Future Star, two albums deep with the label.

artist_notes.name: Ashibah
artist_notes.note: Danish-Egyptian DJ/vocalist on Defected and Get Physical — deep/tech house built around her own live vocals; more pop-house crossover than underground selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Lane 8 and Yotto anchor this fine, but it's a San Diego waterfront day-into-night — factor in the drive. The rest of the bill (Sultan + Shepard, Kasbo, Massane, Qrion) skews toward the melodic/emotive end rather than anything harder.
enrichment.description: CRSSD-affiliated melodic/progressive house day-into-night at San Diego's Waterfront Park, headlined by Lane 8 and Yotto with Sultan + Shepard, Kasbo, Massane, Qrion, Ashibah and Grigore.

artist_notes.name: Gun Outfit
artist_notes.note: Olympia-turned-LA psych/post-punk band on Post Present Medium since their 2008 debut EP — a foundational act for the label being celebrated.

artist_notes.name: The Spatulas
artist_notes.note: Bloomington, IN lo-fi punk band on the Post Present Medium roster.

artist_notes.name: Chronophage
artist_notes.note: Austin DIY punk four-piece with a sophisticated, transgressive songwriting bent — two LPs and a run of cassettes deep.

artist_notes.name: Guiding Light
artist_notes.note: Austin punk band singing bilingually in German/English over jangly, hyper-strummed garage — their debut LP just came out on Post Present Medium.

artist_notes.name: Semi Trucks
artist_notes.note: LA art-pop project fronted by Brendan Sepe, grown from a solo bedroom effort into a full band — scrappy, melodic songs.

artist_notes.name: Muscle Beach
artist_notes.note: LA four-piece delivering noisy, scattershot 'party band' improvisations — a Smell regular.

artist_notes.name: Kate Hall
artist_notes.note: No Age/Mika Miko/Dunes-adjacent LA musician (half of the News Feeds project with Luke Fischbeck & Dean Spunt) DJing the night.

enrichment.curator_note: A real DIY institution's 25th birthday at its natural home — Gun Outfit anchors a bill of scrappy touring bands (Spatulas, Chronophage, Guiding Light) that reads like a Post Present Medium family reunion, not a nostalgia cash-grab.

enrichment.curator_note: Randomer's percussive, textured techno (Hessle Audio/L.I.E.S. pedigree) anchors this, with JKS bringing a harder, more chaotic UK-bass-adjacent set — a real underground techno bill if the TBA venue delivers.

events.detail: Post Present Medium    25 Year Anniversary Celebration, Night III…      Abe Vigoda    Callahan & Witscher ‍  ‍ (NYC)    Debt Rag ‍  ‍ (Olympia, WA)    The Intima ‍  ‍ (Portland, OR)    DREAM_MEGA      Plus DJ Cate Kennan!      8:00 pm    Advance $20 single day tickets available    here   .    Advanc

artist_notes.name: Abe Vigoda
artist_notes.note: LA experimental/'tropical punk' band from the mid-2000s Smell scene, on Post Present Medium — jittery, humid, post-punk-meets-tropicalia; this run is a reunion set for the label's anniversary.

artist_notes.name: Callahan & Witscher
artist_notes.note: NYC duo of two veteran underground experimentalists (Jack Callahan, aka die Reihe; Jeff Witscher, aka Rene Hell) whose new project is a surprising, hooky pivot toward songs after years of noise/ambient work.

artist_notes.name: Debt Rag
artist_notes.note: Olympia, WA punk trio (former members of Grass Widow and Girlsperm) playing guitarless, clattering, drum-and-keyboard punk — Post Present Medium's 2023 LP 'Lost to the Fantasy.'

artist_notes.name: The Intima
artist_notes.note: Portland post-punk quartet, violin-driven, active 1999-2004 and recently reunited — shared stages with The Rapture and The Mekons back in the day; PPM reissued their 'Peril and Panic' LP.

enrichment.curator_note: Three nights deep into Post Present Medium's 25th-anniversary run and this one's genuinely stacked — Abe Vigoda's tropical-punk reunion, Callahan & Witscher's weird new pivot into actual songs, and DIY lifers Debt Rag and reunited Portland post-punk act The Intima. This is the Smell's classic guitars-and-noise lane, not the club side of things.
enrichment.description: Night three of The Smell's Post Present Medium 25th-anniversary celebration: reunited LA tropical-punk band Abe Vigoda, experimental duo Callahan & Witscher, Olympia's Debt Rag, and reunited Portland post-punk band The Intima.

events.title: Mezzanine: Rob Tregenza's Talking to Strangers (1988)

artist_notes.name: Rob Tregenza
artist_notes.note: American structuralist filmmaker — Talking to Strangers (1988) is his triple-threat debut (writer/director/cinematographer): nine unbroken 10-minute 35mm takes, shot once each, sequenced by computer-randomized order. The NYT called it an antidote to jazzy montage; a genuine formalist curio, not a normal narrative feature.

enrichment.curator_note: This is about as structurally radical as rep programming gets — nine single-take, ten-minute 35mm shots, filmed once apiece, no coverage. Not a comfortable watch, but exactly the kind of print/format-driven booking the Mezzanine series exists for.
enrichment.description: 2220 Arts + Archives' Mezzanine series screens Rob Tregenza's Talking to Strangers (1988), a formally radical nine-take 35mm feature.

events.title: Midnight Lovers with Azzecca, Afriqua, Ray Kash

artist_notes.name: Afriqua
artist_notes.note: Adam Longman Parker — Virginia-born, Berlin-based producer on R&S Records; his 2019 LP 'Colored' fused deep house/techno with an explicit Black-culture lens. A genuinely respected, thoughtful name — arguably the most substantive booking on this bill.

artist_notes.name: Azzecca
artist_notes.note: Chicago DJ/producer (Allie DeCastris) and COSIMEA label boss — cosmic, dark, disco-inflected house/techno; a Beatport 'Next Artist' for 2025 who's shared bills with Tale of Us and CamelPhat.

artist_notes.name: Ray Kash
artist_notes.note: LA underground fixture since 2010 (Temple Tuesdays resident) — deep house into techno and melodic, weaned on Danny Tenaglia/Jonathan Peters-style New York house.

enrichment.curator_note: Afriqua alone is worth the trip to DTLA — R&S-signed, one of the more substantive deep house/techno voices around — and Azzecca/Ray Kash round it into a real groove-forward bill rather than another generic warehouse night.
enrichment.description: DTLA club date led by R&S producer Afriqua, with Chicago's Azzecca and LA local Ray Kash.

artist_notes.note: Italian 'Heavy Destroyer' behind TechnoMetal — hard techno fused with metal aggression and industrial noise, co-founder of the HEX movement; his 'Last Resort' hit #1 on Beatport's Hard Techno chart in 2024. artist_notes.note: LA 'second-generation' techno DJ working the local hard/heavy techno circuit (SXTCY, Closer.LA).

artist_notes.note: San Francisco-born, Berlin-based DJ/producer (Eugene Albert) — runs the Limousine Dream label; deep-digging extended sets drifting through minimal house, breaks and hazy late-night rollers.

artist_notes.name: Hazy
artist_notes.note: Recurring Sunday Sessions LA resident — vinyl-only house sets, a regular on the rotation at the series' open-airs.

artist_notes.name: Ian Llorens
artist_notes.note: Certified Groovers resident, LA-based (Puerto Rico-born) — rhythm-forward house/techno selector, also plays as O God / Soundprism.

artist_notes.name: Gilbert0
artist_notes.note: Another Certified Groovers regular — same all-vinyl deep-house lane, secret-location DTLA parties.

enrichment.curator_note: Certified Groovers landing Gene On Earth is a nice get — his Limousine Dream sound is more minimal-and-breaks-leaning than most of the TBA-warehouse bills this month, worth it if you want something a shade weirder than straight house.

events.title: Bonnie Raitt: Live 2026 with Special Guest Jon Cleary
lineup: Jon Cleary & the Absolute Monster Gentlemen
events.detail: Bluesy singer/songwriter Bonnie Raitt has worked long and hard for her multiple Grammy Awards, hit singles and chart-topping records. Since her 1971 eponymous debut, the California-born performer and long-time activist has steadily maintained a music career, albeit with definite peaks and valleys. The red-headed songstress, one of the only women of her time to play guitar using the bottleneck technique, unleashed seven albums in just nine years, though her big commercial break came with her 10th studio set, 1989’s “Nick of Time.” That 11-track collection, produced by Don Was, earned three Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year. Not only has the Rock and Roll Hall of Famer tackled multiple U.S. tours and international runs, but she’s also a frequent participant in events of social activism, such as Farm Aid and Amnesty International concerts. Raitt’s 16th full-length album and most recent studio release, “Slipstream,” hit retailers in 2012. Not only did ticket sales for the support tour soar, but Raitt also landed the best-selling blues album of the year and took home the Grammy for Best Americana Album.
